sources.entry: Solarized - Clean and beautiful color theme. Works well with iTerm, JetBrains products, Vim etc.

summary.name: Solarized
summary.one_liner: Solarized is a sixteen-color terminal and GUI color palette (eight monotones, eight accents) with light and dark modes, created by Ethan Schoonover.
use_cases: Theming a terminal emulator such as iTerm2 or Terminal.app
Applying a consistent color scheme to code editors and IDEs
Syntax highlighting in Vim, Emacs or IntelliJ
Creating five-color palettes for web or design work
Switching between light and dark editing modes with matching contrast
Building custom color themes using the published CIELAB and hex values
summary.what_it_does: Solarized is a sixteen-color palette made of eight monotones and eight accent colors, designed for terminal and GUI applications. The monotones have symmetric CIELAB lightness differences so dark and light modes keep the same perceived contrast, and accent hues are based on fixed color-wheel relationships. The page lists ready-made ports for many editors (Vim, Emacs, IntelliJ IDEA, NetBeans, TextMate, BBEdit, Visual Studio, Xcode in progress), terminal emulators (Xresources, iTerm2, Terminal.app, PuTTY), and palette files for Photoshop, Apple Color Picker and GIMP. It also provides a table of hex, xterm, CIELAB and RGB/HSB values and a sample SCSS snippet for inverting the scheme. Current release is listed as v1.0.0beta2, with the code available on GitHub.
notable: Symmetric CIELAB lightness so dark and light modes have matching perceived contrast
Works as a 16-color terminal palette and scales down to five-color palettes for design
Ports for many editors and terminals, plus Photoshop, GIMP and Apple palettes
Hex, xterm, CIELAB and RGB/HSB value table
caveats: Page notes site restoration in progress
Xcode ports are described as work in progress
TextMate dark theme is work in progress
